bluetooth_no_devices.title: No paired Bluetooth printers found
bluetooth_no_devices.description:
Your Home Assistant host can't see any paired Bluetooth printers. Pair the printer first, then come back to this screen.

**On Home Assistant OS / Supervised**: open Settings → Devices & services → Bluetooth, put your printer into pairing mode, and accept the pairing.

**On Home Assistant Core or Container**: pair from the host shell:

```
bluetoothctl
[bluetooth]# scan on
[bluetooth]# pair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
[bluetooth]# trust AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

If bluez D-Bus isn't reachable from this container (rootless Docker, no `/run/dbus` mount), use the **socat host bridge** described in the [setup guide]({docs_url}). Or if you already know the printer's MAC address, **submit this form** to enter it manually.

Run `bluetoothctl info [MAC]` on the host and look for the SerialPort service-record 'Channel:' line. If you don't have shell access, try 2 or 3.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the network printer. Check the IP address and port (most ESC/POS printers listen on 9100), that the printer is powered on and reachable on the same network, and that no firewall is blocking the connection. If the printer sleeps when idle, try printing once to wake it.
error.cannot_connect_usb: Failed to connect to USB printer. Check that the printer is connected and permissions are configured correctly.
error.usb_permission_denied: Permission denied accessing USB device. On Linux, add udev rules or run with appropriate permissions. On Docker/HAOS, ensure the USB device is passed through to the container.
error.usb_kernel_driver_active: A kernel driver is active for this USB device. Stop other printing services or detach/blacklist the driver (e.g., usblp on Linux).
error.usb_device_busy: USB device is busy. Another application or driver may be using the printer.
error.usb_io_error: USB I/O error while opening the device. This can be transient (reset, autosuspend, or power issue). Try again or replug the printer.
error.usb_device_not_found: USB device not found. Verify the printer is connected and the Vendor ID/Product ID are correct.
error.usb_backend_missing: USB backend (libusb) not found. Install libusb on your system.
error.invalid_line_width: Invalid line width. Must be a positive number.
error.invalid_endpoint: Invalid USB endpoint address. Must be between 0x00 and 0xFF (0-255).
error.cannot_connect_bt: Failed to connect to Bluetooth printer. Verify the device is paired, powered on, and within range.
error.bt_unavailable: Bluetooth Classic (AF_BLUETOOTH/RFCOMM) is not available in this environment. On Home Assistant Container this typically means the container needs '--net=host' and the NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW capabilities. See the README for setup instructions.
error.bt_permission_denied: Permission denied opening the Bluetooth socket. Ensure the Home Assistant process can access bluez (typically requires the 'bluetooth' group on bare Linux).
error.bt_device_not_found: Bluetooth device not found. Pair the printer first using 'bluetoothctl' on the host or HA OS Settings → System → Hardware.
error.bt_host_down: Bluetooth printer is not reachable. Make sure it's powered on, within range, and not currently connected to another host (most BT printers accept only one connection at a time).
error.bt_timeout: Timed out connecting to Bluetooth printer. The printer may be asleep — try printing once to wake it, or increase the timeout.
error.bt_channel_refused: The printer is reachable but refused the RFCOMM channel. Most ESC/POS printers use channel 1 — try a different channel, or run 'bluetoothctl info [MAC]' on the host to confirm the SerialPort service-record channel.
error.invalid_bt_mac: Invalid Bluetooth MAC address. Expected format AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.invalid_rfcomm_channel: Invalid RFCOMM channel. Must be between 1 and 30.
error.cannot_connect_serial: Failed to connect to serial printer. Check that the port exists and permissions are configured correctly.
error.serial_permission_denied: Permission denied accessing serial port. On Linux, add the Home Assistant user to the 'dialout' group (sudo usermod -aG dialout homeassistant).
error.serial_port_not_found: Serial port not found. Verify the port path or URL is correct.
error.serial_port_busy: Serial port is busy. Another process may be using it.
error.invalid_baudrate: Invalid baud rate. Select one of the supported rates.

calibrate_confirm.title: Calibrate printer
calibrate_confirm.description: This wizard prints a series of test pages to measure your printer's image implementation, paper width, characters per line, and character encoding — using roughly 15–20 cm of paper in total. Make sure paper is loaded before continuing.

calibrate_impl.title: Calibrate: image implementation
calibrate_impl.description: Your printer just printed three numbered test patterns. A working pattern is a crisp checkerboard; a failing one prints stray letters or nothing. Check every pattern that printed cleanly. If none of the patterns printed cleanly, leave all boxes unchecked — the width test will be skipped since it needs a working image mode.

calibrate_width.title: Calibrate: paper width
calibrate_width.description: Your printer just printed five numbered bars. Bars wider than your printer's true width get cut off at the same length. Counting from the top, pick the first bar that is the SAME length as the bottom bar. If the bars look like staircases rather than clean solid blocks, choose Not sure — your printer wraps rather than clips.

data.first_equal: First bar equal to the bottom bar

calibrate_ruler.title: Calibrate: characters per line
calibrate_ruler.description: Your printer just printed a ruler of dots, with a digit every 10 columns (10, 20, 30...) and a '|' every 5. Find the LAST marker that printed fully before the line wrapped or ran off the paper, and enter its column number (e.g. if the '4' at column 40 is the last one that fully fits, enter 40). Enter 0 if you're not sure.

data.last_marker: Last marker that fully fit (0 = don't know / skip)

calibrate_codepage.title: Calibrate: character encoding
calibrate_codepage.description: Your printer just printed one numbered line per candidate encoding, each attempting to render "{sample}", the ideal text. Check every line whose printout matches its own expected text shown in the checkbox label — including any ? marks. A line that prints exactly what its label shows is a working codepage. If none match, or you'd rather leave the character encoding unchanged, choose "Skip this step".

data.codepages_match: Lines that match their own expected text

profile_width_fallback.title: Printer profile is missing the pixel width
profile_width_fallback.description:
The selected printer profile ({profile}) does not expose `media.width.pixels`, so images are being scaled to a generic {fallback}px width. This is usually correct for 58 mm thermals but may print stretched or truncated on 80 mm printers.

**To fix:** open the integration's options and set “Paper width in pixels” (384 for 58 mm, 576 for 80 mm printers), pick a closer matching printer profile, or set `image_width` explicitly in your service calls.

print_text_utf8.description: Print UTF-8 text with automatic transcoding to printer codepage. Select one or more printer devices as the target.

broadcast.description: Explicitly print to every configured printer. Mutually exclusive with device_id. Omitting both device_id and broadcast also targets all printers (kept for backward compatibility), but logs a warning when more than one printer is configured — set broadcast: true to make the intent explicit and silence it.
